title: Jai Anjaneya
body: Anjaneya or Hanuman stands as a symbol of Shakti and Bhakti in Hindu Mythology. Shakti means physical strength combined with the courage and initiative to use it for good and Bhakti is true, selfless devotion to God. The scriptures define Shakti and Bhakti to be critical components of a perfect human and Hanuman is a perfect example.

He is stronger than Vajra (Lord Indra’s mighty thunderbolt) and faster than Vayu (The Wind God – His adopted father). He has innumerable boons from the Gods as a result of heroic acts He performs all through His life but He continues to maintain great humility.

He is the principal devotee of Lord Rama (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu). When Rama's wife, Sita (an incarnation of Maha Lakshmi) disappears, He plays a major role in the search and finds Her in Lanka in the grasp of Demon King, Ravana. An entire chapter of Ramayana is devoted to the heroic deeds of Hanuman. This is called the Sundara Kaandam. The scenes where He flies across the seas to give hope to Sita that Ram will come is iconic. He acts as Rama’s messenger and advises Ravana to send Sita back. When infuriated Ravana tries to set fire to His tail, Hanuman ends up burning all of Lanka in His rage. He stands with Rama as His general in the fight between Good and Evil and wins with Rama’s name on His lips and heart. Once when His devotion to Lord Rama is questioned, He tears open his chest to show Lord Rama and Sita sitting there. Can you imagine a bigger superlative of devotion?

As a gift for fighting and winning the war on Lanka, Hanuman requests to stay with Rama forever. Even today, in all temples dedicated to Lord Rama, Hanuman is placed opposite Lord Rama with praying hands.
closing: Blessed are the ones who have a strong, completely devoted friend by their side! Let’s all learn to be each other’s rock!
